values.note: No opened document states a glass content for 'NU-LHT' as a product. Design values are per member: Stoeser 2010 Table 6 (printed p. 7) 'LHT-1M 80 16 4' and 'LHT-2M 65 30 5' (crystalline/agglutinate/good glass %), i.e. 20 % and 35 % glassy components. The only 40 % glass figure found is for a different product: Slabic 2024 p. 22 'The crystalline to glass ratio for NUW-LHT-5M is 60:40.' Rickman 2013 Table 4 gives 39.88 vol% total glass for NU-LHT-1M by SEM (includes pseudo-agglutinate glass). Likely mis-attribution.

No document states a release year for the series. Circumstantial: Rickman 2024 (PDF p. 49) cites 'Stoeser, Douglas B., and Steve A. Wilson. "NU-LHT-1M: Pilot Highlands Soil Simulant," 38. Huntsville, AL, 2007'; He 2010 cites Stoeser et al. (2008) 'The LHT (Lunar Highlands Type) regolith simulant series' (GSA 2008); Patzwald 2025 says 'In the late 2000s'.

values.quote: While there were still scattered supplies of JSC-1A and BP-1 lunar mare simulants, the NU-LHT supply of lunar highlands simulants was about spent.
values.note: Categorical mapping: document says supply 'about spent' (2024). Corroborated by Stockstill-Cahill 2022 p. 38 'The NU-LHT series is not currently in mass production' and Patzwald 2025 p. 203 'The series is currently not being produced.'

values.quote: The two dominant rocks in the NU-LHT simulants were Anorthosite and Norite from the Stillwater Mine in Nye, Montana, with the primary purpose of creating a noritic anorthosite simulant like the Apollo 16 regolith samples (see Figure 12).
values.note: Series-level statement. Also Stoeser 2010 p. 1 for 1M/2M.

values.quote: Besides JSC-1A, there is another NASA-produced simulant series [NASA/U. S. Geological Survey - Lunar Highlands Type (NU-LHT) and its derivatives] for highland soils
values.note: Stored string carries a stray carriage return ('\r'). MSFC involvement is stated in Stoeser 2010 p. 1: 'In discussions with the Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), it was agreed that the first prototype regolith simulants produced by the United States (U.S.) Geological Survey (USGS) would simulate the lunar highlands regolith'.

results.notes: S047 'NU-LHT' is the family/series name (NASA USGS-Lunar Highland Type), not a distinct product; every document uses it only as a series label ('NU-LHT series', 'NU-LHT and its derivatives'). The database already holds the members 1M (S049), 1D (S048), 2M (S051), 2C (S050), 2E (S086); 2EG, 3M, 4M and NUW-LHT-5M also exist (Slabic 2024 pp. 19–22). Recommend converting S047 into a family record or merging. R041 (Duri 2022) has local_path null but the paper is on disk at papers/Duri_etal_2022_Regolith_Simulants_Plant_Growth_Review_FrontAstronSpaceSci_8_747821.pdf and papers/LRS/Duri et al. - 2022 - The Potential for Lunar and Martian Regolith Simul.pdf (identical text); it only lists the family in Table 1 with no property values and cites Stoeser et al. 2010a and Zeng et al. 2010. The stored glass 40 % most plausibly comes from NUW-LHT-5M (60:40). The stored institution value has a trailing '\r'.

results.notes: R042 has local_path null but the TM is on disk at papers/Stoeser_Rickman_Wilson_2010_NU-LHT-1M_2M_NASA-TM-2010-216438.pdf (byte-identical to papers/LRS/20110008071.pdf). The stored citation says '(2011) ... pp. 1-13'; the document itself is dated August 2010 (NASA/TM-2010-216438, 24 pp). Stoeser 2010 contains design specifications only (target Apollo 16 chemistry, feedstocks, mixing ratios, <1 mm size) and no measured properties of the product. Two independent oxide analyses exist for 1M: Rickman 2013 Table 3 (Preliminary Certificate: SiO2 47.62, Al2O3 24.4, CaO 13.1, MgO 8.5, FeO 3.3/Fe2O3T 4.79, Na2O 1.43, TiO2 0.33, K2O 0.08) and Rickman 2024 Table 4.4 (USGS XRF: SiO2 47.30, Al2O3 24.00, CaO 13.60, MgO 8.66, Fe2O3 4.91, Na2O 1.42, TiO2 0.34, K2O 0.09, Cr2O3 0.12, MnO 0.08; Table 4.5 FeO 2.33; Table 4.6 C 0.03, S 0.01). Two modal datasets differ (Schrader 2010 QEMSCAN vs Rickman 2013 SEM); both are listed. Rickman 2013 Table 5 feedstock proportions for 1M: Norite 30, Anorthosite 43, Harzburgite 6.1, Ilmenite 0.72, HQ glass 3.96, Pseudo-agglutinate 15.9 %. Rickman 2013 p. 48: 'Size analysis of NU-LHT-1M indicates that 13% of total volume is <20 µm.' Rickman 2024 Table 8.1 BET specific surface area for 1M: 0.6505 m2/g (JSC) and 1.366 (Alfred). Patzwald 2025 wrongly assigns Twin Sisters dunite to 1M; Stoeser 2010 Table 3 assigns it to 2M and Stillwater harzburgite to 1M.

Space Res. 43, 448-454, doi 10.1016/j.asr.2008.07.006 — no local copy; paywalled (DOI landing = Elsevier redirect shell, ScienceDirect and NASA ADS returned bot-challenge pages, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar: closed, abstract elided). Only bibliographic metadata saved: papers/agent-fetched/Crossref_metadata_Zheng_2009_CAS-1_ASR_43_448.json, OpenAlex_Zheng_2009_CAS-1.json, SemanticScholar_Zheng_2009_CAS-1_abstract.json
results.notes: (1) The primary source Zheng et al. 2009 (R008 = R096, duplicate references to the same DOI) could not be opened; every CAS-1 number above is a secondary reproduction that itself cites Zheng 2009 (Li et al. 2022 Table 1/2/4, simulantdb, Alberquilla 2022 Table 2). Values agree across Li 2022, simulantdb, Chen 2025 Table 3 and Alberquilla Table 2 (rounded: 'CAS-1 49.2 1.9 15.8 0.1 8.7 7.3 – 11.5 3.1 1.0 0.3 98.9'). (2) Mineralogy is a CIPW norm; simulantdb states it 'does not account for the glass content (20-40%)'. (3) Geotechnical conflict: Ruan et al. 2024 Table 7 lists CAS-1 friction angle 39.84–41.09° and cohesion 2.8–5.00 kPa versus 33.3°/1.0 kPa from Zheng 2009 as reproduced by Li 2022 and simulantdb; source of Ruan's CAS-1 column is not stated in the text I read. (4) Several sources (Patzwald 2025, simulantdb, Global Registry citing Tang 2017) say CLRS-1 is probably another name for CAS-1, and CLDS-i is derived from CAS-1. (5) The 'Global Registry of Lunar Regolith Simulants' page in papers/LRS/Sources is a CSV compilation with no author; its columns (Release Date 2009, Replica of Apollo 14, Stage Available) match the stored scalars and it is probably the origin of the stored release_date/lunar_sample_reference; it should not be cited as a source. (6) Library documents listed for CAS-1 were all opened; all name CAS-1. The TJ-1 ResearchGate page (files/1765) mentions CAS-1 only inside citing-article snippets, not in the TJ-1 abstract. (7) Chen et al. 2025 also report CAS-1 'circularity values of about 0.66 and aspect ratios of about 1.5 ( Zheng et al., 2009)' — no matching DB column.

results.notes: R026 (Taylor et al. 2005, MetSoc abstract 5180) is about JSC-1, not JSC-1A: it never uses the name JSC-1A and only says 'As the initial supply of 27 tons is now dwindling, new production has commenced.' It should be moved to JSC-1 (S027) rather than kept as a JSC-1A usage reference. R087 could not be opened, but He 2010 (NEW4) Table 3.7 (PDF p.151) tabulates Alshibli et al. values for JSC-1A: D10 0.016, D30 0.043, D50 0.090, D60 0.120 mm, rho_max 2.016, rho_min 1.566 g/cm3, Gs 2.92, e_max 0.877. Three of the stored geotechnical numbers (bulk_density 1.63, cohesion 1.9, friction_angle 45.85) are not stated in any opened document and look like interpolations of ranges on the NASA ARES page; a curator should replace them with sourced values (e.g. He 2010 Table 3.6 friction angles 41.9/46.5/56.7° at 1659/1789/1940 kg/m3; Engelschiøn 2020 bulk density 1.56 g/cm3). Mineralogy is contradictory between sources: Coker 2026 / ARES page give Glass 49.3, Plagioclase 37.1, Olivine 9.0 wt%, whereas Slabic 2024 Table 5 (PDF p.42, citing Schrader et al. 2008, OCR garbled) gives 'JSC-lA 26.67 19.4 3 37.83 12.44 0.1 1' (Glass 26.67, Pyroxene 19.43, Plagioclase 37.83, Olivine 12.44, Ilmenite 0.11). Rickman 2024 Table 4.4 gives two further JSC-1A XRF analyses (UTSA: SiO2 46.71, Al2O3 16.07, Fe2O3 12.54 ...; USGS: SiO2 46.80, Al2O3 16.40, Fe2O3 12.70 ...). Orbitec MSDS Section 3 gives oxide ranges for the family (SiO2 46-49, Al2O3 14.5-15.5, Fe2O3 3-4, FeO 7-7.5, MgO 8.5-9.5, CaO 10-11 ...). The bgtech review (NEW15) attributes a JSC-1A oxide row to 'Wang et al., 2022', which may be the untraceable R027 citation used for JSC-1AC.

results.notes: R102 has local_path null in the group file but is present locally as papers/LRS/JSC2A-zocca2020.pdf. Both stored particle-size entries derive from Zocca's sieved study fractions (<20 µm and <100 µm), not from the as-received product, and the stored range '2.3-102 µm' splices two fractions; neither should stand as a bulk JSC-2A PSD. 'Production stopped' contradicts every opened source, which present JSC-2A as the current replacement for JSC-1A. Zocca notes JSC-2A 'is produced following a different synthesis method' from JSC-1A and that 'JSC-2A contains a significant amount of amorphous phase [14]' (glass not quantified). Ramos Somolinos 2024 measured JSC-2A at a compacted bulk density of 1.73 g/cm3 (PDF p.8) and permittivity ε′ = 3.53 at 9.375 GHz; Engelschiøn 2020 p.5 reports glass transition 620 °C and crystallisation peak 800 °C for both JSC-1A and JSC-2A. The bgtech review gives JSC-2A sintering start 1160 °C and softening 1216 °C; Zocca Table (p.7) gives sintering start/softening/ball/half-ball/flow points for the two sieved fractions (e.g. <100 μm, 50 K/min: 1091/1124/1161/1216/1316 °C).
